synopsis: The booklet recommends ACARP Tier 1 and Tier 2-style controlled whole-machine tests after high-throughput regression, covering worst-case stopping, grades and loads, target classes, nuisance braking, mixed motion, sensor obstruction, and generated adverse environments where feasible [f749]. It identifies access to ACARP and Mining3 methods, MOSH specifications, test sites, a qualified independent body, and traceability as critical inputs for shared frameworks and independent review [f1057]. However, it states an ACARP limit: shared frameworks, third parties, and independent review cannot by themselves establish site-specific, multi-variable dynamics [f1055]. A separate glossary example describes a University of Queensland–ACARP project using a haul-truck simulator around 2017 to evaluate visual and sound proximity interfaces; that work addressed advisory warnings, not automatic braking [f13405].

relations.note: Whole-machine testing addresses dynamics that frameworks and independent review alone cannot establish.
Identifies critical inputs for the frameworks and review whose site-specific limits are stated.
